# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

- **The reserved-band lint (AC-AA-78, AC-AA-108) has unproven feasibility.** The spectral-centroid and band check on imported assets may be too noisy to gate on; the tag-only lint plus the blind tests is the MVP default and the spectral lint a Vertical Slice upgrade (OQ-AA-5, CD-GDD-ALIGN). The band half of AC-AA-78 is advisory until the spike lands.
- **Audible latency is a measurement, not a rule.** "Audio no later than visual" is proved as an ordering guarantee (AC-AA-5, AC-AA-110); the device-buffer and Windows-stack delay is a spike (AC-AA-6).
- **The deaf and hard-of-hearing tell channel is the visual rim plus the opt-in haptic beat pulse (AA-42).** No criterion can make a tell audible to a player who cannot hear; the ruled substitute is the beat pulse (AC-AA-149, AC-AA-112), and the criteria assert that no other setting adds one (OQ-AA-15 resolved). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
- **Spikes AC-AA-6, AC-AA-80 and AC-AA-81 close on a recorded result.** AC-AA-80 and AC-AA-81 carry thresholds; AC-AA-6 does not and cannot until the first measurement exists.
- **Panel feasibility.** Every `(manual)` criterion needs the panel protocol; if a 5-tester panel cannot be had, the criterion is closed as "indicative" only (OQ-AA-13).
- **Criteria on provisional reads** (AC-AA-33, AC-AA-93, AC-AA-95 against stubs; AC-AA-55, AC-AA-57, AC-AA-60, AC-AA-61, AC-AA-62, AC-AA-109 against the Filter transport) are attributed to the neighbour when they fail and re-run at the X-6 confirming scan.
- **Pod and body assets (AC-AA-53)** are wired at MVP and authored at Vertical Slice; the criterion passes with a placeholder or no asset, which proves the wiring only.

I'm counting roughly 160 acceptance criteria checked so far, and now I'm drafting new rows to add, starting with test infrastructure covering a headless request-capture harness, a dev-build audio tap bus for capturing effects pre-fader, and CI performance budgets.

From there I'm sketching boot-time data-relation validation that refuses booting on invalid relations, latency handling for AUDIO_LEAD_MS against unobservable device buffer delay, a spike on combining AudioStreamPlayer2D with AudioListener2D inside a fixed SubViewport (checking pan fallback, listener placement, max distance, and de-click timing), and same-frame request ordering guarantees across announcement, strike, and breach events within a single poll.

Then I move to event name binding validation so every consumed key matches its owner's published name and fails boot otherwise, cross-system provisional read stubs like beacon_live debouncing for alarm grid mode selection, and finally footfall driven by published odometer/gait/octant/facing data rather than the Presenter's internal animation counter.

I skip several narrower duplicates — annunciator T_e state (not covered by TR-002's memory list but too narrow to pursue), voice allocator determinism (subsumed by the deterministic stealing order item), and haptic feedback (covered by TR-027) — before landing on a new item: output device loss and return, covering the audio_output_lost diagnostic, sustained resume behavior, non-replay of one-shots, and unchanged state hash.

I add master peak headroom (sub -3 dBFS triggers a warning diagnostic), the pinned 48kHz mix rate, and a new audio asset budget row checking total assets against AUDIO_ASSET_BUDGET_MB. I also fold in a small new rule that no presenter or shader symbol reads Audio directly, keeping dependency flow one-way, and note that BODY_* events are published but shouldn't register as Attention stimuli.

For dev-build diagnostics, I decide the various DIAGNOSTIC counters (tier-1 steal, drops, peak warnings, output loss) don't need their own row since they're already folded into row 042. Then I move to co-op networking concerns — listener_scope addressing, OWNER_PRIVATE routing, and dead-seat handling — deciding to include a row covering per-seat local audio derived from replicated state and peer-seat cue triggers, tied to the ADR-0032 replication requirement.

Then I check mute-invariance (already covered) and bus tree structure — confirming the voice bus carries no DSP, only vox, one per family, and no Area2D overrides — and decide to include that as its own row. I'm finalizing the remaining rows (031-041) and tallying roughly 160 ACs total.

| TR-audio-032 | Every cross-knob data relation (D.6 bed margin, D.8 radius and floor budget, D.10 pool sizes, D.11 reach pre-roll, D.13 creak density, D.19 audibility and peak relations, D.9 log-law radius) is checked at data load; hard relations refuse boot, soft relations log a DIAGNOSTIC, and a DIAGNOSTIC failing at shipped defaults counts as a failure. | Data | AC-AA-9, AC-AA-11, AC-AA-17, AC-AA-31, AC-AA-46, AC-AA-66, AC-AA-134, AC-AA-146 | ADR-0007 |

| TR-audio-035 | When one poll holds several simultaneous facts, requests are created in a fixed order (annunciator, strike, BREACH_ENTER), each on a free or reserved voice with none dropped, and every audio request frame is at or before the first visual draw frame of the same event. | Threading/Timing | AC-AA-26, AC-AA-110, AC-AA-132 | ADR-0029 + ADR-0001 |
| TR-audio-036 | Every dirty key, view field and event name that Audio consumes must match the owning system's published name exactly, and an unknown name fails boot; Audio registers no subscription to a name absent from the owner's inventory. | Core | AC-AA-88, AC-AA-33, AC-AA-93 | ADR-0004 + ADR-0029 |
| TR-audio-037 | The alarm clock mode (ALIGNED or FALLBACK) is chosen at `breach_enter_T` + 14 from a debounced `beacon_live_f` (Emitter BEACON on the home-ship body with `output_pm` > 0 held `BEACON_LIVE_HOLD_TICKS`, listener on that body), changes only at pulse boundaries, and is immune to read toggling. | Threading/Timing | AC-AA-95, AC-AA-133 | ADR-0017 + ADR-0029 |
| TR-audio-038 | Footfalls are driven only by published odometer, gait, octant and facing, never by a Presenter `anim_counter`; `FOOT_CONTACT_FRAMES` is exported from the character sidecar, not coded; restore primes the counter and a catch-up poll fires at most one footfall. | Core | AC-AA-49, AC-AA-122, AC-AA-152 | ADR-0019 + ADR-0029 |
| TR-audio-039 | An output-device loss and return emits one `audio_output_lost` DIAGNOSTIC per loss, replays no one-shot that fell inside the loss, resumes sustained cues at steady level with de-click, and leaves `state_hash` unchanged. | Audio | AC-AA-155 | ADR-0029 |
| TR-audio-040 | The Master bus peak stays below -3 dBFS in the worst-case scene over a 10,000-frame soak (`master_peak_warn` is 0), and the total shipped audio asset size is under `AUDIO_ASSET_BUDGET_MB` with the `wit` asset count capped at `WIT_MVP_ASSET_CAP`. | Performance | AC-AA-135, AC-AA-134, AC-AA-111 | ADR-0029 + ADR-0007 |
| TR-audio-041 | The bus tree maps each family to exactly one bus, the `Voice` bus carries only `vox` and has no DSP, no sanity, stage or Filter input and no duck from a `hal` cue, and no `Area2D` `audio_bus_override` is used for routing. | Audio | AC-AA-63, AC-AA-86, AC-AA-89 | ADR-0029 |
| TR-audio-042 | No presenter or shader symbol reads Audio, and no visual parameter references an audio level, bus meter, cue start or voice state, so the visual twin never depends on audio and audio-driven flashes, vignettes or camera nudges cannot exist. | Rendering | AC-AA-118 | ADR-0009 + ADR-0029 |
| TR-audio-043 | In co-op, each client derives its own cues from replicated published state: peer-seat P1 cues use `listener_scope` ALL_EXCEPT_SOURCE and trigger on `tell_on`, no bed request is addressed to a dead seat, and a source seat never hears its own cue; the contract is dormant at MVP. | Networking | AC-AA-62, AC-AA-116, AC-AA-109 | ADR-0032 |
